title: U.S. House · Texas's 29th Congressional District
area: East Houston, including parts of the Houston Ship Channel area.

context.text: Texas redrew its congressional district boundaries in August 2025 ahead of the 2026 elections, a mid-decade redistricting.
In the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary, incumbent Sylvia Garcia defeated Jarvis Johnson and Robert Slater, 58.2% to 35.7% to 6.1%. Martha Fierro was unopposed for the Republican nomination.

summary.text: Sylvia Garcia is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for Texas's 29th District, in office since 2019. A social worker and lawyer by training, she was presiding judge of the Houston municipal court system, Houston city controller, a Harris County commissioner, and a Texas state senator before Congress. She is Vice Ranking Member of the House Financial Services Committee.

background.text: Born in San Diego, Texas, in 1950; according to her congressional biography, she grew up in the farming community of Palito Blanco as the eighth of ten children.
Earned a bachelor's degree in social work and political science from Texas Woman's University in 1972 and a J.D. from Thurgood Marshall School of Law at Texas Southern University in 1978.
Worked early in her career as a social worker and a legal aid lawyer.
Served as director and presiding judge of the Houston Municipal System for five terms under two mayors, according to her congressional biography.

Elected Houston city controller in 1998 and served two terms, then was elected to the Harris County Commissioners Court, where her biography says she was the first Hispanic and first woman elected in her own right.
Sworn into the Texas Senate on March 11, 2013, representing District 6, after winning a special runoff election for the seat of the late Sen. Mario Gallegos; she served until 2018.
Elected to the U.S. House in November 2018 and sworn in January 3, 2019, becoming the first Latina to represent the 29th District.
Serves as Vice Ranking Member of the House Financial Services Committee; in January 2020 she was one of seven House managers in the Senate impeachment trial of President Trump.

positions.summary: Campaign issues page says she is fighting to pass the Women's Health Protection Act to safeguard access to safe, legal abortion.
positions.quote: she is fighting to pass the Women’s Health Protection Act to safeguard access to safe, legal healthcare, abortion, and IVF

positions.summary: Official site says she supports gun safety legislation and is a member of the Gun Violence Prevention Task Force.
positions.quote: Congresswoman Garcia supports gun safety legislation

positions.summary: Campaign issues page says she is pushing back against cuts to Medicaid and Medicare.
positions.quote: She is pushing back against Trump and his billionaire allies who put corporate profits ahead of people, slashing Medicaid, Medicare, and programs that help families make ends meet.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Financial Services and the House Committee on Ethics in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Martha Fierro
candidates.ballotNote: Unopposed for the Republican nomination in the March 3, 2026 primary

summary.text: Martha Fierro is the Republican nominee in Texas's 29th District. Describing herself as a pastor, nurse-trained small business owner, wife and mother of five, she has run unsuccessfully for the Texas Senate and Texas House in earlier cycles and is running on affordability, public safety and border security.

background.text: According to her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, she was born in Matamoros, Mexico, came to the United States at age seven, was raised in Texas, and is a naturalized citizen.

Describes herself as a first-generation college graduate who earned an associate degree in nursing and bachelor's degrees in Human Development and Family Studies and Psychology from the University of Houston (2016); she also received an honorary Ph.D. from Paragon Christian University in 2026.
Describes herself as a pastor and small business owner who has been married more than 32 years and has five children.

Ran as the Republican nominee for Texas State Senate District 6 in the December 2018 special election (23.2%, behind Carol Alvarado), for Texas House District 145 in 2020 (lost to Christina Morales), and for Texas Senate District 6 in 2024 (lost to Alvarado).
Advanced from the March 3, 2026 Republican primary for the 29th District.

priorities.text: Her campaign website lists making healthcare more affordable, expanding educational freedom, making Houston affordable by cutting federal spending, and securing the borders.

statements.quote: Expand educational freedom and strengthen family values. Empower parents with school choice, defend parental rights, and protect the values that make Texas strong.

statements.quote: By raising competition, expanding access, and protecting patient choice — not imposing government mandates — we can ensure families and seniors get the care they need at prices they can afford.
statements.context: On her campaign website, under "Protecting Healthcare Access"

statements.quote: Public Safety, Secure Our Borders! Support Border Patrol and stop policies that encourage illegal crossings and human trafficking.
statements.context: On her campaign website, under "Defending Our Rights"
